sources.name: Astronomy Engine
sources.producer: Don Cross / CosineKitty
sources.role: Topocentric apparent Sun and Moon positions and angular radii, optional planet positions, plus ideal-horizon sunset, calculated in the browser.
sources.coverage: Point calculations for user-provided terrestrial coordinates.
sources.resolution: Analytical ephemeris calculation; project documentation states accuracy within approximately one arcminute.

license.name: MIT

sources.attribution: Astronomy calculations by Astronomy Engine.
sources.transformation: The application supplies latitude, longitude and an effective observer elevation equal to IGN/CNIG TerrainRGB ground elevation plus an explicit 1.5 metre planning viewpoint height. The engine's Delta T hook selects the IERS Bulletin A value for 2026 and the NASA/GSFC long-range prediction published with the 2027 or 2028 element table. Apparent Sun and Moon positions are evaluated at the contact and maximum instants supplied by the owned Besselian local-circumstances implementation. The optional chart context evaluates Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn at the selected instant and observer. SearchRiseSet supplies the apparent upper-limb sunset against an ideal horizon using its documented standard refraction; the result is not a terrain or obstacle sunset. Astronomical output remains unknown when ground elevation cannot be resolved.
limitations: Results must be validated against an independent official source before they are used for a release recommendation.
The 1.5 metre viewpoint height is a planning assumption, not a measured tripod, eye or instrument height for an exact venue.
A positive apparent solar-centre altitude does not establish terrain, building or vegetation clearance at that contact.
Optional planet labels show calculated positions only and do not establish naked-eye visibility during an eclipse.

sources.name: Besselian elements for the total solar eclipse of 12 August 2026
sources.producer: Fred Espenak / NASA Goddard Space Flight Center
sources.role: Published polynomial elements used by the owned browser implementation to calculate local contacts, maximum, eclipse type, magnitude, obscuration and totality duration.
sources.version: NASA/GSFC Solar Eclipse Search Engine page updated 2023-10-30; VSOP87/ELP2000-82 elements centred on 18:00 TDT.
sources.coverage: Local circumstances for the 12 August 2026 total solar eclipse during the published 15:00–21:00 TDT validity interval.
sources.resolution: Polynomial coefficients are retained at the precision exposed by the source page's element data; root solving targets substantially finer internal precision than displayed output.

license.name: Explicit reuse permission with required acknowledgement

sources.attribution: Eclipse Predictions by Fred Espenak, NASA's GSFC.
sources.transformation: The owned implementation evaluates the published x, y, declination, mu, penumbra-radius and umbra-radius polynomials in TDT, transforms the WGS 84 observer into fundamental-plane coordinates, and solves external, internal and maximum roots with safeguarded bisection. The source page's historical 75.4 second Delta T assumption is replaced by the event-specific 69.17309 second value derived from IERS Bulletin A XXXIX-031; TT-UTC remains 69.184 seconds.
limitations: The published elements use the VSOP87/ELP2000-82 ephemeris lineage and are product inputs, not independent verification evidence.
The source notes that path edges are limited by the lunar limb profile; the owned smooth-limb implementation does not predict Baily's-bead timing for a surveyed venue.
A contact time does not establish visibility above local terrain, buildings, vegetation or cloud.

sources.role: Published polynomial elements used by the owned browser implementation to calculate 2027 local contacts, maximum, eclipse type, magnitude, obscuration and totality duration.

sources.attribution: Eclipse Predictions by Fred Espenak, NASA's GSFC.
sources.transformation: The same owned Besselian solver used for 2026 evaluates the event-specific polynomial table and uses the source's 76.0 second Delta T prediction. Regression tests compare Cádiz, Ceuta and Málaga durations with the IGN published city summaries.
limitations: The NASA elements are product inputs and are not independent verification evidence.
The smooth-limb calculation does not predict Baily's-bead timing for a surveyed venue.
The long-range Delta T value must be replaced with final Earth-orientation data for a post-event scientific archive.

sources.role: Published polynomial elements used by the owned browser implementation to calculate 2028 local contacts, maximum, eclipse type, magnitude, obscuration and annularity duration.
sources.version: NASA/GSFC VSOP87/ELP2000-82 elements centred on 15:00 TDT; published Delta T 76.3 seconds.
sources.coverage: Local circumstances for the 26 January 2028 annular solar eclipse. The published coefficient fit covers 12:00 to 18:00 TDT.

license.name: Explicit reuse permission with required acknowledgement

sources.attribution: Eclipse Predictions by Fred Espenak, NASA's GSFC.
sources.transformation: The same owned Besselian solver evaluates the event-specific polynomial table and uses the source's 76.3 second Delta T prediction. The Spanish C4 search continues the published polynomial by 15 minutes because the partial phase leaves western Spain shortly after the stated six-hour fit interval. Regression tests compare the end time with the IGN published 19:08 CET end and check the roughly seven-minute annularity in Sevilla, Córdoba and Valencia.
limitations: The NASA elements are product inputs and are not independent verification evidence.
Spanish C4 uses a short continuation beyond the stated coefficient-fit interval and must be replaced by a later event-specific reference before a rigorous 2028 release claim.
The long-range Delta T value must be replaced with final Earth-orientation data for a post-event scientific archive.

sources.name: IERS Bulletin A XXXIX-031
sources.producer: IERS Rapid Service/Prediction Center, U.S. Naval Observatory
sources.role: Event-specific Earth-rotation and civil-time inputs used to derive TT-UTC and Delta T for 12 August 2026.
sources.coverage: MJD 61264 (12 August 2026): TAI-UTC 37 s, TT-TAI 32.184 s and predicted UT1-UTC +0.01091 s.
sources.resolution: Daily published prediction. Derived TT-UTC is 69.184 s and Delta T is 69.17309 s.

license.name: No explicit reuse licence identified in the cited bulletin; source attribution retained

sources.attribution: Earth-orientation prediction: IERS Rapid Service/Prediction Center.
sources.transformation: TT-UTC = (TAI-UTC) + (TT-TAI). Delta T = (TT-UTC) - (UT1-UTC). The derived event value configures Astronomy Engine and the owned Besselian hour-angle calculation.
limitations: The 12 August UT1-UTC value was a prediction when the bulletin was issued and should be refreshed from a later final IERS product for a post-event scientific archive.
The implementation does not currently apply the bulletin's polar-motion values; their omission is recorded as a model limitation rather than silently inferred.

sources.attribution: Información astronómica oficial ofrecida por el Instituto Geográfico Nacional siguiendo los cálculos realizados por el Observatorio Astronómico Nacional.
sources.transformation: An offline deterministic generator verifies the frozen COG checksum and metadata, crops source pixels without reprojection or interpolation, renders band 1 as apparent solar-centre altitude in degrees and band 3 as obscuration percentage with quantity-specific palettes, masks no-data and maximum-after-sunset cells, and publishes only lossless PNG files with a versioned manifest and checksums. Altitudes below 0 degrees and obscuration below the displayed 80 percent domain are transparent visual cutoffs, not reclassified values. A versioned tolerance of 0.00002 is applied only to the colour index for small band-3 floating-point excursions; scientific values are not rewritten.
limitations: The overlay is visual regional context and does not expose or imply an exact value at a clicked coordinate.
The altitude describes the apparent solar centre at maximum and is not a terrain-clearance or whole-disc horizon result.
The obscuration layer is not magnitude, weather probability, viewing quality or a recommendation.

sources.name: Official 2026 eclipse vector package
sources.producer: Instituto Geográfico Nacional / Observatorio Astronómico Nacional
sources.role: National totality-duration ranges and discrete umbra-passage frames.
sources.coverage: EPSG:4326 totality-duration polygons and umbra footprints for the 12 August 2026 eclipse, cropped by the runtime map viewport.
sources.resolution: 13 duration ranges from 0–10 through 120–122.7997 seconds; 277 umbra footprints from 18.293 to 18.569 decimal UTC hours at 0.001 hour (3.6 second) intervals. The upstream shadow layer declares a 0.0001-degree simplification.

license.name: CC BY 4.0-compatible IGN/CNIG data policy

sources.attribution: Información astronómica oficial ofrecida por el Instituto Geográfico Nacional siguiendo los cálculos realizados por el Observatorio Astronómico Nacional.
sources.transformation: An offline deterministic generator verifies the frozen byte size, SHA-256, EPSG:4326 MULTIPOLYGON schemas, feature counts, duration-range continuity, timestamp flags and 3.6 second cadence. It rasterizes duration polygons at EPSG:3857 output pixel centres and applies the rasterized union of all 277 same-package umbra footprints as a totality-envelope mask, retaining the official 0–10 second edge band while making cells outside totality transparent. Umbra rings receive an additional 1/120-degree Douglas–Peucker simplification only when relative ring-area error remains at or below 1 percent, then coordinates are rounded to six decimals. Polygon shapes are never interpolated. Upstream IDs, layer names, time-flag columns and absolute producer paths are removed; only UTC hours and coordinates are published in a checksum-bound JSON artifact.
limitations: Duration colours represent official ranges and are not an exact point value.
Umbra frames are discrete samples; playback selects the nearest frame and does not infer intermediate polygon topology.
An umbra footprint means totality at the sampled instant, not cloud, ambient brightness, weather or terrain shadow.
The additional simplification is suitable for national visualization, not boundary surveying or point classification.
This package shares IGN/OAN eclipse lineage with the official raster and does not count as an independent ephemeris or unlock a recommendation.
The source GeoPackage is not redistributed by the application.

sources.name: TerrainRGB XYZ service
sources.producer: Instituto Geográfico Nacional / Centro Nacional de Información Geográfica
sources.role: Western terrain-horizon profile calculated directly in the browser.
sources.version: Service observed 2026-08-02; source dataset version not asserted by the application.
sources.coverage: Configured request envelopes intended to cover the Iberian Peninsula, Balearic Islands, Ceuta, Canary Islands and Melilla; the service determines pixel-level data availability.
sources.resolution: Zoom 11, 512 × 512 pixel TerrainRGB samples; ground resolution varies by latitude and is approximately tens of metres.

license.name: CC BY 4.0-compatible IGN/CNIG data policy

sources.attribution: TerrainRGB XYZ service, accessed 2026-08-02 · CC BY 4.0-compatible · © Instituto Geográfico Nacional de España.
sources.transformation: The application requests https://xyz-mdt.idee.es/1.0.0/raster-dem/{z}/{x}/{y}.png. RGB values are decoded with elevation = -10000 + (R × 256² + G × 256 + B) × 0.1; transparent and out-of-range pixels are rejected as no-data. It starts with 61 profile rays across 30 degrees around the peak solar azimuth and expands the 0.5 degree profile grid when needed to cover the C1-to-C4 solar track, spherical disc width and one degree of interpolation padding. A separate local solar-disc sweep has no azimuth gap wider than 0.05 degrees. The model adds an explicit 1.5 metre planning viewpoint height, applies Earth curvature and a documented standard refraction coefficient, and reports geometric terrain-disc intersection without a quality score.
limitations: The terrain model does not represent current vegetation, temporary structures or every building.
The model is a planning aid and cannot replace an on-site horizon photograph or survey.
The current profile samples to 100 km at discrete distances and azimuths and can still miss features between samples.
The rectangular request envelopes are not Spain's political boundary, include neighbouring territory and sea, and do not guarantee a valid elevation pixel.
The Step 6 TerrainRGB-to-MDT05 residual sample contains five mainland points, including one targeted nearby coastal pair, and is not evidence of Spain-wide accuracy.

sources.name: ERA5 August evening cloud-cover climatology
sources.producer: Copernicus Climate Change Service / ECMWF; delivered by Open-Meteo
sources.role: Checksum-bound historical cloud-cover context for the 41 national planning references.
sources.version: ERA5 1991–2020 August sample; public artifact era5-august-evening-v1; SHA-256 3d85c8128b2c029103eb5547b5be06605245330b7f7ec9edff23171a09678b6f.
sources.coverage: The 41 independently sourced national reference points displayed by the clean Spain-wide map.
sources.resolution: ERA5 0.25 degree nearest grid cell; 930 hourly samples per point at 18:00 UTC, comprising every August day from 1991 through 2020.

license.name: Open-Meteo API data under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; upstream Copernicus licence retained

sources.attribution: ERA5: Copernicus Climate Change Service / ECMWF. Historical API delivery: Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0.
sources.transformation: The reproducible scripts/generate-cloud-climate.mts generator requests ERA5 total cloud cover through the Open-Meteo Historical Weather API with model=era5, UTC, nearest-cell selection and no statistical downscaling. It validates 30 annual responses, rejects missing or out-of-range values, calculates the mean and 25th, 50th and 75th percentiles at each reference, records an aggregate SHA-256 for the 30 locally retained raw responses, and publishes only the compact versioned JSON artifact and checksum.
limitations: This is reanalysis climatology, not a forecast for 12 August 2026 and not a probability of successful viewing.
A 0.25 degree grid cell cannot resolve site-scale cloud, coastal fog or mountain effects.
The 41 point summaries do not form a continuous Spain-wide weather raster and must not be interpolated into one.

sources.name: ECMWF IFS HRES forecast delivered by Open-Meteo
sources.producer: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts / Open-Meteo
sources.role: Runtime point forecast for cloud layers, precipitation, 10 metre wind and gusts around the eclipse hours.
sources.version: Live ECMWF IFS HRES 9 km model delivery; run metadata is read at runtime and shown beside the result.
sources.coverage: Selected, compared, or nationally displayed reference coordinates when the live upstream service contains the full 17:00 through 20:00 UTC planning window on 12 August 2026.
sources.resolution: Nominal 9 km ECMWF IFS HRES output delivered on an hourly API time series. Native steps become 3-hourly after 90 forecast hours and 6-hourly after 144 hours; Open-Meteo dynamically interpolates them to the returned hourly series. Returned service coordinates and the Open-Meteo downscaling elevation are retained for each point.

license.name: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0

sources.attribution: Weather data by Open-Meteo; forecast model ECMWF IFS HRES.
sources.transformation: The browser validates Open-Meteo run metadata, HTTP status, JSON MIME type, body size, response units, batch location_id identity, array alignment and defensive physical ranges under an eight-second request deadline. It requests a batch for the required locations and selects the four returned hours from 17:00 through 20:00 UTC without adding client-side interpolation. It aligns the hourly display with local C1, central phase, maximum, C4 and ideal-horizon sunset, then shows cloud layers, precipitation, wind and gust from the returned hour nearest maximum. Open-Meteo may interpolate coarser native forecast steps and applies its documented land-cell selection and 90 metre elevation downscaling. The browser first attempts the identified single-run endpoint only when its metadata covers the complete window. Exact-run availability, timeout and transport failures fall back to the explicitly labelled rolling ECMWF endpoint unless the caller cancelled the request. Rolling responses are not pinned to the displayed latest-run metadata and are never labelled as an exact run. Total precipitation is the preceding-hour sum and wind gust is the preceding three-hour maximum. Null, malformed, misidentified, misaligned, out-of-range, unavailable or failed responses remain unknown.
limitations: A single deterministic model does not express ensemble uncertainty and can change materially between runs.
The free Open-Meteo API is non-commercial, rate-limited and has no availability guarantee; production use must satisfy the current service terms.
Runtime values are not archived by the stable scientific report and do not satisfy or unlock the weather release gate.
Nine kilometre model output does not establish the cloud actually present at an exact venue.

sources.role: Independent deterministic total-cloud-cover comparison for the selected location around the 2026 eclipse hours.
sources.version: Live GFS seamless delivery requested explicitly with models=gfs_seamless.
sources.coverage: The selected coordinate when GFS contains the full 17:00 through 20:00 UTC window on 12 August 2026.
sources.resolution: Nominal 0.11 degree, approximately 13 km global surface output. GFS changes from hourly to three-hourly steps after 120 forecast hours, and Open-Meteo interpolates the returned series to hourly values.

license.name: Open-Meteo API data under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; NOAA source attribution retained

sources.attribution: Weather data by Open-Meteo; forecast model NOAA GFS.
sources.transformation: The browser requests only total cloud cover from the dedicated GFS endpoint for the event date. It validates status, JSON MIME type, body size, units, coordinates, array alignment, time ordering and values under an eight-second deadline. It displays the four returned event-window hours in local civil time without client-side interpolation. Missing hours remain unavailable.
limitations: This is one deterministic model, not an independent probability or an ensemble.
The response is rolling delivery and does not expose an exact model-run identity in this interface.
A thirteen kilometre grid and model timing errors cannot establish whether the solar line of sight will be cloud-free at an exact venue.

sources.transformation: The browser requests reverseGeocode for the selected coordinate and keeps only the municipality name and INE code from the response. The service publishes no availability commitment; failures surface as an explicit unavailable state.
